text.p: Luxembourg's Marc Girardelli, five times World Cup champion and winner of more Alpine skiing medals than any other man, announced his retirement at the world championships on Monday.

The Austrian-born all-rounder, who has suffered a string of injuries, said doctors had told him that he could spend his life on crutches unless he stopped racing. "The only thing I have to do now is announce my retirement," he told a news conference.
Girardelli, who has a career total of 13 medals including four world championship golds, has not raced since December and was not competing in Sestriere due to injury.

The 33-year-old, who decided as a teenager to represent Luxembourg after a disagreement with local Austrian skiing officials in his native Vorarlberg, won 46 World Cup races in a career that started in 1980 when he was 18 years old.
He had his first World Cup podium place when he finished second in a slalom in Wengen in 1981 and won the overall World Cup title in 1985, 1986, 1989, 1991 and 1993.

Girardelli's career has also been hit severely by injury and he has undergone 13 major operations. He almost died in 1989 from internal bleeding following a heavy crash in a super-giant slalom in Sestriere.
